newsitem.title: UK: MFI lifted by Carpetright comments.
newsitem.headline: MFI lifted by Carpetright comments.

text.p: Shares in household goods retailer MFI Furniture Group Plc gained on Tuesday after floorcoverings group Carpetright Plc said sales growth had been encouraging since the start of May, dealers said.
MFI shares rose 5p to 140p by 0925 GMT, while Carpetright climbed 39-1/2p to 480-1/2p after reporting pre-tax profits of 32.2 million stg, in-line with analysts' expectations.
Dealers said Carpetright's comments were being interpreted by investors as the beginning of a recovery in demand for consumer durables.

Carpetright said store sales had risen four percent in the seven weeks since the general election. It suggested its carpet business might benefit from some of the windfall cash gained by consumers from the demutualisation of building societies such as Halifax and Alliance and Leicester.

MFI shares have been under a cloud since the group issued a warning on March 4 that its second-half sales growth was lower than that achieved in its first half. The shares reached their year low of 120p on May 23.
Also in the sector, Allied Carpets was up 5-1/2p at 230 and Kingfisher Plc was up 4-1/2p at 730-1/2.
However, analysts remained cautious on the prospects of an increase in demand for consumer durables in the near term.
"There is no strong evidence of a boom in demand developing," said one analyst.
"Although in the past month there was a certain amount of relief that the hiatus of the election was over."
MFI are due to report full year results on July 1.
